title: At noncritical affine-sl2 level, the explicit twisted de Rham complex on the punctured line embeds as a shifted subcomplex of current-algebra chains with tensor contragradient Verma coefficients
author: Alexey Slinkin; Alexander Varchenko
source_title: Twisted de Rham Complex on Line and Singular Vectors in sl(2) Verma Modules
difficulty_reason: Compatibility of the de Rham differential with the current-algebra action requires nontrivial affine-Verma identities at every pole order, not just agreement on logarithmic one-forms. The authors prove those identities by evaluating all PBW basis types and controlling higher-current commutator cancellations, then use them in both the finite-point and infinity expansions of the chain map. The injection remains valid at resonant highest weights, while the noncritical level and shifted degrees are essential.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The entire Theorem4.1 proof and the essential new identities of Theorem3.2 were read, including every PBW-basis group O/I/II/III in Section5. The chain-map proof explicitly compares all finite-pole and polynomial basis terms, using the separately proved contragradient-Verma current identities. The support proof supplies the affine diagram involution, dual action formulas, graded-degree vanishing, the full multi-Cartan induction and two-current cancellations; no announced-only identity is treated as proved background. The earlier Schechtman–Varchenko announcement is credited, but the full human proof used here is this article. Both degrees of the injection and the noncritical-level condition are retained. No separate singular-vector resonance consequence is counted.

statement_scope: Exactly Theorem4.1: z_1,...,z_n are pairwise distinct complex points, U=C minus these points, k,m_1,...,m_n are complex with k+2!=0, kappa=k+2 and m_{n+1}=sum_{j=1}^n m_j-2. V_j is the affine-sl_2 Verma module V(m_j,k-m_j), with the restricted graded contragradient V_j^*. The source current algebra consists of sl_2-valued rational functions regular on U, acting by Laurent expansions at the finite points and by the specified pi automorphism at infinity. The exact maps(4.2)-(4.5) give an injective homomorphism from Omega^bullet(U)[1] with differential d-(1/kappa)*sum_j m_j*dt/(t-z_j) wedge to the Chevalley–Eilenberg chain complex with tensor_{j=1}^{n+1} V_j^* coefficients; the degree-zero and degree-minus-one terms satisfy d*eta^0=eta^1*partial. No irreducibility or nonresonance of the Verma modules is assumed, and no assertion at k=-2 is selected.
editorial_warning: The final sentence calls the injective maps eta^1 and eta^2, while the construction defines eta^0 and eta^1; these are the two maps selected. In Section5.1 some module subscripts print m-k while the displayed highest-weight generator and diagram involution use k-m; the actual explicit map and both identities are included unchanged. These bounded naming slips are distinguished from the author proof and no rewritten current identity is substituted.
source_boundary_note: The complete original Theorem 4.1 and its finite-pole/polynomial chain-map proof are retained. The noncritical level, both shifted degrees, restricted contragradient Verma modules, current action at finite poles and pi-twisted infinity action, and all four explicit eta formulas are included. The source new current identities of Theorem 3.2 are not assumed background: their complete Section 5 proof, with every O/I/II/III PBW-basis group, diagram involution, dual action and multi-Cartan cancellation, is supplied as uncounted new core. The prior announcement is credited. Singular-vector/resonance consequences are not separate counted outcomes, and the original eta/module naming slips remain unchanged.
